nodes.label: Build the verifier before the generator
nodes.rationale: The source document's headline thesis is already true here: one validateAssignments is shared by the greedy placer, the drag-drop board and both AI runners, and effectiveRestMinutes exists precisely so those callers cannot disagree about what a rule means. The value in the source material is therefore its gap list, and every gap was reproduced against this repo before being accepted.

nodes.label: computeParticipants (set-valued)
nodes.rationale: The highest-leverage single change: toEngineAssignments derives people from [home, away] non-null, so a TBD slot carries nobody and 10 of 13 badminton fixtures constrain nothing. Reading pack.participants instead makes every person rule fire on elimination brackets for the first time. Set-valued (not the source's singular personOf) because an entrant is a team — copied as-is it would drop every roster member but one.

nodes.label: One organisation timezone governs all temporal math
nodes.rationale: Day boundaries are otherwise undefined across zones, so 'two matches per day' has no single answer. Per-division tz becomes display metadata. Accepted cost: sessionHours becomes organisation-zoned, so a Malaga division under a London org shifts an hour; explicit sessionWindows are absolute instants and are the documented escape hatch. J6 is rewritten rather than extended — the one place the joint prompt is not purely additive.

nodes.label: Calendar anchor: clock + window + sentinel kill
nodes.rationale: SchedulePack has no clock and no window, so a division with no configured start emits 1970-01-01 draft timestamps to the model and, with empty sessionWindows, nothing bounds output dates — 03:00 verifies clean. `now` is always injected, never read, so the double-seed golden-pack determinism test stays green.

nodes.label: Stage-1 instruction compiler (schedule-ai-parse)
nodes.rationale: The organiser's instruction is never verified today, so 'two matches per day' or 'final on Friday' cannot converge in repair rounds. Schema-forced with symbolic dates only and one retry; a double schema failure hard-fails at the preview rather than silently falling back, because a silent fallback would present a rule as enforced while nothing enforces it. `unparsed` renders verbatim and is never converted into a rule.

nodes.label: Parse runs outside spendCredit
nodes.rationale: The preview introduces an abort point that did not previously exist, so parse runs as pre-flight with its own small meter and ~1K clampRound; the reservation happens when the organiser confirms. This keeps 'one credit, one architect run' literally true and makes walking away free. Abuse exposure is ~400 output tokens per abort behind the existing rate limit. Consequence: parse spend sits outside quote.budget and needs its own ledger stamp line or it is invisible.

nodes.label: Delta-based blocking
nodes.rationale: person_overlap is only a warning today, so a human booked on two courts at once applies and publishes. Blocking only conflicts a change introduces or worsens keeps a dirty board editable; pre-existing conflicts pass through as warnings and only newly introduced ones 409. Requires a stable conflict identity, reusing the existing ${fixtureId}|${reason}|${detail} key.

nodes.label: Scheduling-only name guard (synthetic PersonKey)
nodes.rationale: Over-constrain the schedule, never the database: a false merge costs one unnecessary rest gap, a false split books one human on two courts — but merging two real people corrupts stats, discipline history, photos and consent. The key never leaves the pack, is recorded in assumptions, and disappears once registration auto-link makes the real person_id shared. It covers every registration including anonymous ones, which is why it carries the load the deferred cause fix cannot.

nodes.label: Duplicate person_ids are a write defect, not a read defect
nodes.rationale: The schema and the scheduler's read are correct; registrations unconditionally insert a person per confirm with no lookup, and entrants.ts states non-merging as policy. contact_email is not a safe join key — a guardian registering two children uses one address, so auto-linking would merge siblings, which is worse than the bug. No safe key exists on the anonymous public-registration path today, so the cause fix is deferred and only the persons(org_id, user_id) partial unique index is enforceable in the database.

nodes.label: Rule codes on Conflict (one vocabulary)
nodes.rationale: The prompt teaches H1–H7 / J1–J7 while the verifier reports {reason:'rest'}, so a repair round hands the model a word it was never taught. The mapping is fixed, exhaustive and defined once beside the ConflictReason union rather than at each call site; no_slot has no rule code because it is the capacity case and carries CAP.

nodes.label: Feeder rest (gap 7), deliberately sequenced into W4
nodes.rationale: A dependent fixture may start the instant its feeder ends, so the advancing player gets no recovery. Though it needs nothing from W2 or W3, adding +effectiveRest would make previously legal boards emit blocking conflicts and any subsequent edit would 409 — safe only once delta-based blocking can let a pre-existing violation through as a warning.

nodes.label: z3 minimal-movement repair (W6)
nodes.rationale: Sequenced last because its encoding cannot exist before the window and the typed constraints do. Owner decision: no fixture-count gate — higher latency on large boards is acceptable; the binding constraint is termination, so a finite wall-clock solver budget falls back to LLM repair with the fallback visible in telemetry. z3 requires no data-protection work: it is an in-process WASM library, not a sub-processor — hosted solvers were rejected.

nodes.label: Placement rule: pure primitives in packages/engine
nodes.rationale: Every pure new primitive lands in packages/engine (zod only — no DB, no provider, no wall clock); usecases keeps only the impure parts. This is what gives the solver its safety property: the verifier and the solver import one implementation of every rule semantic and therefore cannot disagree.

nodes.label: Test both directions (rejection AND acceptance)
nodes.rationale: A verifier that only rejects is untested where it matters most. Fixtures are the two real production payloads, frozen; the golden pack is updated exactly once per wave as a deliberate reviewed diff so churn cannot hide a real change. The guardian anti-merge test (one contact_email → TWO persons rows) is a permanent regression guard against ever making the name guard a record merge.
